I admit that I was momentarily hooked. trying again and again to finish the first level, and once i reached the first boss, I saw the big ugly flaw in this game's design for leveling design. After maximizing the upgrades I can get for my armor and gun, and unlocking half of all possible unlocks available to me, I cannot muster the DPS needed to hardly get the FIRST BOSS down by just a quarter of his health before the game kills you automatically, since you are only granted 90 SECONDS to beat the boss. The game wants to go full send on the DPS to kill the boss in time, but if you dont level your health, you wont even make it to the boss, and there is only so much DPS you can get and its at the whim of RNG. The one thing this game did accomplish is that I will no longer be tempted by those stupid mobile ad versions this game was trying to emulate.

While interesting, the game's pacing is very slow and drawn out. It's also a terrible resource hog. It'll only work on certain Proton versions, and choosing the wrong Proton version will hard lock the system. Also, when closing it out, it will never cleanly close and figuring out just which process is still running and registering is beyond me. While it's a good attempt at what it does, it has too many technical and mechanical issues to pull it into a recommended category.

[quote][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asset_flip]Warning: Asset Flip![/url][/quote] [quote][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_slop][b]Warning: AI Slop[/b][/url] This game is partially or completely made with talentless, soulless AI generated content.[/quote] "Wacky West" is I guess a little more than just a minimum viable product, this looks like a mostly genuine effort to create a hybrid between an endless runner and a ripoff of Vampire Survivors (copyright Poncle, 2021), that looks like it was made out of a bunch of Synty assets with AI slop for the UI. What do you do in the game? Gameplay cosnsists of endless running down a Space Invaders like street while bullet helling through enemies with your auto-attacks, and picking up Vampire Survivors like upgrades. I've seen worse, but this is winning no awards and the use of AI slop is an insult to everyone. While I couldn't find this on the mobile app stores, everything about it looks and feels like it's a mobile app designed for mobile phones... for PC gaming enthusiasts, it's not going to give you a cutting edge PC gaming experience. That alone is enough to disqualify this from any recommendation. We don't spend thousands building gaming rigs so that we can pretend they're iPhones and play iPhone games and mobile apps. As mentioned, this features really godawful, "wrong" looking AI slop instead of genuinely and sincerely created game assets. It's hard to say if this was because the developer didn't have the skill to do the job of creating real game assets or couldn't afford to hire someone who does, but it also doesn't matter. What matters is that this looks bad because of that decision. AI slop sticks out like a sore thumb... and it comes across as insulting. Edit: The developer has now confessed that he's plagiarised a bunch of Synty assets and put his own name on them to try get famous for the work of others. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. Now on to pricing and value for gamers. This is "free" enough (not every "free" game in the "free" section is truly free, there's usually some hidden price tag), at least you won't be expected to spend any more money after you download this, but just because something is free doesn't mean it's good, and the cost of a game is more than just financial, your time is valuable too. In terms of public reception, this failed to appeal to the 130 million+ gamers on Steam. SteamDB showed the game peaked at just a dozen or so concurrent players, and now there's basically nobody playing it. Even though it's free. This is a dismal public reception, but it's easy to see why gamers rejected it. Given that this free title won't increase your game collector count, is it worth your time to add it to your library? I think you should give this one a miss. Although it's free, your time and storage are valuable resources, and the market is filled with superior options. The use of AI slop is a direct insult to gamers and real, ethical content creators and artists everywhere. [quote][url=https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/reviews]Developer Response![/url][/quote]The developer has weighed in to inform everyone they didn't read the [url=https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/reviews]Developer Usage Rules[/url] for Steam "partners", or they deliberately ignored the part where Valve says: [quote]Though it may be tempting, not every review needs to be responded to. A developer response will frequently draw more attention than the original statement, potentially turning a small issue into a much larger community discussion. It's also not a good idea to use this feature to refute customer opinions. Your direct attention can be seen as validation or a defensive attempt to silence your customers.[/quote] The developer churns out a bunch of lies, dishonesty and direct misrepresentation of the facts, to mislead gamers. This response is absolutely deplorable. Let's break down the lies, and lies they are. First the developer claims there's no AI Slop. Here's the store page blurb that the developer wrote that proves this to be a lie! [quote]Some of the non-gameplay related placeholder 2D illustrations/icons are made using AI[/quote] Lying isn't smart, and it's downright stupid when the facts that prove you're lying are right there and in your own words. We've learned so much about this garbage, failed developer already. The developer outright ADMITS this is an asset flip, he took a bunch of other people's assets and put his own name on them... disgusting plagiarism. And like I said, the quality of this garbage was indistinguishable from an asset flip... well now we know it's just outright plagiarism. Unethical, morally and creatively bankrupt. The developer pushes the lie that this is somehow successful, it's not. SteamDB does not lie, the peak player counts were tiny, bad even for a "free" asset flip, and the ongoing activity on the game is next to ZERO. Anyone can look at SteamDB and once more see the developer is quite simply spreading bullcrap to try cover for his failure. Absolutely unacceptable behaviour from a developer who's proven to be utterly dishonest in the face of the facts. The developer whines that the truth is hateful. Telling gamers the truth is hate, now? Telling the truth to gamers is the highest calling when reviewing games, good or bad. When someone is offended by the truth about harmful, morally bankrupt and highly unethical plagiarism, that should be a point to stop and perhaps wake up and see the harm their amoral, harmful lies and plagiarism causes. This disgusting attitude from a failed developer is exactly why amateur developers have such a bad name. Nothing in the developers pointless breach of Valve guidelines changes any of the objective facts of my review. I have amended this review to more properly warn gamers that this is in fact nothing but a garbage asset flip. I cannot recommend this failed asset flip to anyone. Edit: The developer DEMANDS that "art" cannot be criticized. WTF? The guy didn't even make the art, he stole Synty's art. And I think Synty assets are crap to start with. The developer essentially demands that unless a review is an empty participation trophy full of love for the Synty assets he stole and put his name on, it cannot be posted. This is a complete insult to the intelligence of every gamer everywhere. There are no falsehoods in my review. There's no "bad faith" in telling the truth. The developer makes libelous, false accusations, trying to make this review about me instead of his garbage plagiarism (which the Wikipedia article I link about asset flips clearly classifies this garbage as). And the developer has the gall to insult the true heroes of game development, the real, professional game developers (as opposed to talentless, amateur hacks who can't make a game without stealing someone else's work) who work hard, long hours and endure crunchtimes to release those hugely successful games that gamers actually play. 95% of Steam revenue comes from 5% of the games, but this guy is so self-absorbed he refuses to accept that gamers like quality, and not asset flips like this garbage.

The game doesn't look bad but why a negative review? I had to go through the beginning of the game three times. The first time I fell into nothingness, the second one threw me off and I couldn't figure out the ending because it already let me into the game itself when I played it for the third time. The game lags, when I reduced the resolution to minimum the lag completely disappeared. It's more likely a bug, the game is hardly that heavy. I know it's a free game, but there are bugs and bad balance at times, and the explanations could be better. The game still needs some repair. I passed all the levels and the game has no end to the story. You can literally beat the game with just the first weapon. And the side upgrades. Makes other weapons useless. And diamonds too. There is not much difference between the bosses and the enemies in general need more variety. Also, balance, I died several times on the first level, passed the second only twice, the third once, and the fourth with the first time, and I lucked out because I had the bomb spell that killed the last boss with one hit. It doesn't have to be harder, but more balanced. The endless level is also pointless because you start from nothing and it takes a long time to start collecting resources and even more time for them to change. By the time I reached the second resource, the enemies were too strong. The other four levels are easier to find resources. Several new bugs also appeared. The game has potential but needs some repair, it looks like early access.

I stumbled across this gem by chance and have to admit, it's worth checking out, especially considering that it's free and a small-scale project. In terms of level design, the idea of using bosses as DPS checks is a pleasant challenge given the short lenght of one run. The idea of granting perks for a certain number of upgrades is also great and adds a new layer of decision-making. In terms of upgrades, there are plenty and almost every single one of them fells impactful when you purchase them and start a new run. Just like the weapons, one of which supports you during the run, that can also be upgraded in between. Each one provides a different playstyle and the visualisation is realy neat. At this point I'm not far enough into the game to see if there is an endless mode, but I’m sure there will be. The only minor drawback, or perhaps just an idea, is that: at the start of a run the first selection could have a fixed rarity. This the level of rarity (aka stars) could then be adjusted through an upgrade like the gear and weapons. Otherwise one might be inclined to restart runs over and over to get a 'better' start. All in all a well made game that's fun to play. Hold it up, Devs :)
